sentence: Our ride is Voyager 1, the farthest thing we've sent.
claim: Voyager 1 is the most distant human-made object from Earth.
source_title: Voyager 1 will be 1 light-day from Earth on November 17-18, 2026 (EarthSky)
note: Excerpt: Voyager 1 is currently the most distant human-made object from Earth.

source_title: NASA's iconic Voyager 1 marks 45 years in space (Space.com)
note: Excerpt: launched on September 5, 1977, weeks before its twin Voyager 2.

sentence: It coasts at about seventeen kilometers a second.
claim: Voyager 1 moves away from the Sun at about 17 km/s (about 38,000 mph).
source_title: The Nearest Star (NASA Goddard, Imagine the Universe)
note: The bible's source (§7 #6, 'at about 17 km/s'). In this session the figure was seen in search excerpts quoting NASA's Voyager 1 mission page (38,026.79 mph, about 17 km/s relative to the Sun, Aug 2024, via Space Daily) and Fox News (38,000 mph); the Goddard page itself was not opened. 'Coasts': it has made no major burns since its planetary encounters. The six hours is c4's (26 Oct: one number per sentence, after the script audit).

sentence: Earth to the Moon in six hours.
claim: The Moon's mean distance from Earth is 384,400 km; at Voyager's 17 km/s that takes about 6.3 hours.
note: Distance from the bible (§7 claim 3). Computed: 384,400 km / 17 km/s = 22,612 s = 6.28 h ('six hours').

sentence: On November eighteenth, it crosses a line.
claim: NASA gives the moment Voyager 1 reaches one light-day from Earth (about 25.902 billion km, 173.14 AU) as 2:16:07 a.m. PST (10:16:07 UTC) on Wednesday 18 November 2026.
source_title: Voyager 1: What Is a Light-Day? (NASA Science)
note: 26 Oct (script audit): the time was wrong here. EarthSky's '12:16:07 a.m. CST' (06:16 UTC) does not match NASA's 2:16:07 a.m. PST = 5:16:07 a.m. EST = 10:16:07 UTC (search excerpts this session: NASA's page via a search summary; astrobiology.com's event listing, 5:16:07 a.m. EST); EarthSky's figure looks like a PST conversion slip. The URL is the one the audit's searches returned; open it before posting. One light-day = 299,792.458 km/s × 86,400 s = 25.90 billion km = 173.14 AU. Post at or after 10:16 UTC on 18 Nov if possible (before that the signal is short of a day by about a second). Present tense: true on the post date.

sentence: Its signal now needs a full day to reach us.
claim: A light-day is the distance a signal at the speed of light covers in 24 hours; at one light-day, Voyager 1's radio signal takes about a day to reach Earth.
source_title: Voyager 1: What Is a Light-Day? (NASA Science)
note: Bible §7 #6 source. Also: JPL's Suzy Dodd, via CNN (kvia.com, 9 Dec 2025): a light-day is the distance light covers in 24 hours. Radio travels at the speed of light.

sentence: The answer comes the day after tomorrow.
claim: At one light-day, a command takes about a day to reach Voyager 1, and the team waits another day for its response.
source_title: Voyager 1 will reach one light-day from Earth in 2026. Here's what that means (CNN, via KVIA)
note: Excerpt: after sending a command, the team would wait another day for a response. 'The day after tomorrow' = about 48 h after sending.

sentence: In twenty twelve, it crossed into interstellar space.
claim: Voyager 1 crossed the heliopause, the edge of the Sun's solar-wind bubble, into interstellar space on or about 25 August 2012 (announced September 2013), about 18.2 billion km from the Sun.
source_title: At last, Voyager 1 slips into interstellar space (Science News, 2013)
note: A University of Maryland model put it in July 2012; NASA's fact sheet says July/August 2012. 'The Sun's wind' = the solar wind; 'interstellar space' in NASA's sense (the plasma between stars), not beyond the Sun's gravity or the Oort cloud.

sentence: It hasn't even reached the Sun's cloud of comets.
claim: Voyager 1 has not yet reached the Oort Cloud, the theorised shell of icy bodies (comets) around the Sun, whose inner edge is thought to lie about 1,000–5,000 AU from the Sun (Voyager 1: about 173 AU).
note: Excerpt: Voyager 1 will take about 300 years to reach the inner boundary of the Oort Cloud. NASA: the Oort Cloud is theoretical (no object observed in the distant cloud itself); the picture badges it 'theory'. NBC News (JPL team): 200–300 years.

sentence: That's about three hundred years away.
claim: Voyager 1 will take about 300 years to reach the inner boundary of the Oort Cloud.
note: Excerpt from the NASA page; NBC News quotes the JPL team: 'another 200 to 300 years'. 26 Oct (script audit): 'about' restored, as NASA writes it; the figure is the low end of NASA's range for a cloud nobody has observed (badged 'comet cloud: theory').

sentence: Through it: maybe thirty thousand more.
claim: Voyager 1 will probably take another 30,000 years to exit the far side of the Oort Cloud.
note: Excerpt: 'probably another 30,000 years to exit the far side'. Also NASA's 'Solar System perspective' image article ('possibly about 30,000 years to fly beyond it'). 26 Oct (script audit): 'maybe' restored (NASA: 'possibly about 30,000 years'); the high end of NASA's range.

sentence: The nearest star, Proxima Centauri, is about fifteen hundred light-days out.
claim: Proxima Centauri, the nearest star to the Sun, is about 4.24 light-years away: about 1,549 light-days.
source_title: Our nearest celestial neighbor: an exotic 3-star system (NASA Science)

sentence: At Voyager's speed: about seventy-five thousand years.
claim: At Voyager's speed (about 17 km/s), reaching Proxima Centauri at its present distance would take about 75,000 years (NASA's rounder figure: 'over 73,000 years').
source_title: The Nearest Star (NASA Goddard, Imagine the Universe)
note: Computed: 4.24 ly × 9.4607e12 km / 17 km/s = 2.36e12 s = 74,800 years ('about seventy-five thousand'). NASA Goddard (quoted by Space Daily): 'it would take over 73,000 years to arrive' (from about 17.3 km/s). Proxima is approaching (radial velocity about −22 km/s), so the figure holds Proxima at today's distance; the picture badges 'at today's distance'. Voyager is not headed toward Proxima (it heads for Ophiuchus); the line says 'at Voyager's speed' and the drawn direction is badged.

sentence: Count back that far, and our species wasn't in Europe.
claim: No Homo sapiens are known in Europe 75,000 years ago. Earlier claims did not last or are disputed: Apidima 1, Greece, at least 210,000 years (Harvati et al., Nature 2019; date and species disputed), and Grotte Mandrin, France, about 54,000 years (a short incursion; Neanderthals returned). Our species' lasting presence starts a little over 45,000 years ago (Bacho Kiro; ancient DNA, Nature, Dec 2024).
source_title: Oldest human DNA reveals family network that spanned Europe (University of Bristol, Dec 2024, on Nature 2024)
note: Excerpt: early modern humans arrived as small groups in Europe more than 45,000 years ago. 'That far' = the 75,000 years of c12. The Mandrin date (about 54,000) comes from general knowledge, not from a search excerpt in this session; it doesn't change the claim. An archaeologist may prefer a primary source. 26 Oct (script audit): 'hadn't reached' stated a contested first arrival as settled (Apidima 1); 'wasn't in' states presence 75,000 years ago, which every side accepts. Apidima: University of Tübingen press release (search excerpt this session), https://uni-tuebingen.de/en/newsfullview-landingpage/article/earliest-known-homo-sapiens-in-eurasia-found-in-greece/ ; de Lumley disputes it (Neanderthal, about 160,000 years).

sentence: Voyager has crossed day one of fifteen hundred.
claim: Voyager 1 is about one light-day from Earth; Proxima Centauri is about 1,549 light-days away.
source_title: Voyager 1 will be 1 light-day from Earth on November 17-18, 2026 (EarthSky)
note: Computed from c5 and c11: day 1 of about 1,550.

sentence: Light time, Earth to Voyager: one day.
claim: Light from Earth reaches Voyager 1 in about one day (from 18 November 2026).
source_title: Voyager 1: What Is a Light-Day? (NASA Science)
note: The closing light-time readout (the channel's recurring segment). Same as c6.

sentence: To Proxima Centauri: four years and three months.
claim: Light from Proxima Centauri takes about 4.24 years to reach us: about 4 years and 3 months.
source_title: Our nearest celestial neighbor: an exotic 3-star system (NASA Science)
note: Computed: 0.24 years × 12 = 2.9 months ('three months'). The readout says 'Earth to Voyager', then 'to Proxima Centauri' (from the Sun; the difference is 8 light-minutes).

sentence: Next: a world that turns slower than it orbits.
claim: Venus takes 243.0 Earth days to spin once relative to the stars and 224.7 days to orbit the Sun: it turns slower than it orbits.
note: Bible §7 #2. Sidereal rotation 243.0 d vs orbital period 224.7 d. Sunrise to sunrise is 116.75 days; episode 3 explains it. The tease avoids 'its day is longer than its year' (the reviewer's point: the solar day is shorter than the year).

claim: Venus rotates retrograde (backwards relative to its orbit and most planets' spin).
note: The fact sheet lists the sidereal rotation period as −5832.6 hours (negative: retrograde). NASA Space Place: the Sun rises in the west there. 26 Oct (script audit): the end card now says 'a planet that turns backwards' (not 'the planet'): Uranus also rotates retrograde (NASA, quoted by Africa Check: 'Like Venus, Uranus rotates in the opposite direction as most other planets'; https://africacheck.org/fact-checks/fbchecks/no-venus-not-only-planet-rotates-clockwise, search excerpt).
